title: It began with air mattresses in 2007.
description:
It began with air mattresses in 2007. Brian Chesky and Joe Gebbia rented out space in their San Francisco apartment during a design conference, charging $80 a night, to help pay their rent.

It was called AirBed & Breakfast. The site, airbedandbreakfast.com, launched on 11 August 2008. It was shortened to Airbnb in March 2009 to eliminate confusion over air mattresses.

They sold political cereal at the 2008 conventions. Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's, sold mostly at the Democratic National Convention, according to Wikipedia. ProductHabits says roughly 500 boxes of each were made, planned at $40 a box.

The sum reported as raised by selling cereal. Wikipedia, Benzinga and ProductHabits all give it, though none quotes the founders directly.

Paul Graham doubted anyone would use it. ProductHabits says he was sceptical but backed the founders themselves. Y Combinator took them on in January 2009 for $20,000 and a 6 per cent stake, per Wikipedia.

The shortened name, by which point the site had 10,000 users and 2,500 listings, according to Wikipedia.

Cereal boxes first. Then 10,000 users.

Sources:
